findings: Server serialize() emits the US spelling "canceled" (single L) for sub.canceledAt truthy case, and also for sub.status when it presumably equals "cancelled" — but the documented contract requires the value "cancelled" (UK spelling, double L); the client's isCancelled() checks `sub.status === "cancelled"`, which will never match "canceled", so the cancelled banner never appears — this is the root cause of the QA bug.

The server's ternary `sub.canceledAt ? "canceled" : sub.status` returns the misspelled "canceled" literal when canceledAt is set, instead of the contract-compliant "cancelled", regardless of what sub.status itself contains.

When canceledAt is falsy, the server passes through the raw `sub.status` value unmodified/unvalidated — if the internal/domain model's status enum differs from the documented client-facing enum ("active"|"paused"|"cancelled"), e.g. uses different strings internally, the contract is violated with no normalization layer.

Server returns `amount: sub.amountCents`, i.e. a cents-denominated integer, while the documented contract specifies `amount: number // dollars`; the client's formatAmount() does `sub.amount.toFixed(2)` assuming the value is already in dollars, so the displayed price will be shown as 100x too large (e.g. $1999.00 instead of $19.99) with no unit conversion anywhere in the pipeline.

There is no shared/generated type or schema (e.g. no shared TS interface, no OpenAPI/JSON-schema validation, no contract test) enforcing that server output matches the documented contract, so the spelling and units mismatches were not caught at compile time or by any automated check.

The comments in client.ts ("UK spelling, matches the documented contract" and "assumes dollars, per the documented contract") assert conformance to the contract without any verification against the actual server implementation, indicating the mismatch was introduced/missed via unchecked trust in comments rather than actual validation.
